e1e441f9b8db1a901975d76a0b70e0f5c6ba0efc7089663b62d492eb869830c1 --- [[00_论文总目录|70篇总目录]] · [[00_全文_02_GEO方法优化_目录|本类完整稿]] · [[02_GEO小白实操教程_从选问题到验证效果|实操教程]] 原论文：[固定版本](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.07315v2) · [[11_White Hat Search Engine Optimization using Large Language Models.pdf|本地PDF]] # 使用大语言模型进行白帽搜索引擎优化 **原题：White Hat Search Engine Optimization using Large Language Models** **作者：**Niv Bardas、Tommy Mordo、Oren Kurland、Moshe Tennenholtz、Gal Zur；以色列理工学院，海法。 **版本：**arXiv:2502.07315v2，2025年2月23日，5页。页眉残留“Conference’17, July 2017, Washington, DC, USA”，与arXiv版本日期不符，本稿不据此认定发表于2017会议。 **状态：**全文中文初校，包含全部正文、3张表、2个提示词图、公式、脚注与参考文献题名；未复现实验。本文研究的是**检索排序改稿**，不是生成式回答中的引用份额，归入GEO库是为了学习相邻方法。 ## 第一部分：论文全文中文译文 ### 摘要 我们提出基于生成式AI的新颖白帽搜索引擎优化技术，并用实证结果展示其价值。 ### 1 引言 在竞争性搜索环境[10]中，文档作者看到感兴趣问题的排名后，可能修改自己的文档，希望改善未来排序。这些修改通常称为搜索引擎优化 SEO[8]。与先前竞争性搜索工作[6,10,19]一样，本文关注白帽 SEO：不损害文档质量和搜索生态的正当内容修改。 我们提出用于临时查询检索（ad hoc retrieval）的文档修改方法，以提示大语言模型实现。期望[6]包括：可能提升当前查询的后续排序；保持对原文的“忠实”；生成高内容质量的文档。部分方法受利用LLM提示来生成查询排序的研究[11,12,18]启发。例如提示中加入历史排名所提供的信息，让LLM间接了解未公开的排序函数。 我们在先前排名竞赛数据[13,19]上评估，还组织排名竞赛，让改稿方法作为机器人与人类竞争。结果显示，最有效方法相对于人类及一个很强的特征式文档修改方法[6]具有优势。 **脚注1：**作者称竞赛数据和代码将在论文发表后公开；审稿阶段可访问 https://github.com/promptdriven2025 。这是原文发布说明，本稿没有核实该仓库当前状态。 **相关工作。**竞争性搜索综述见[10]。最相关的是 Goren 等[6]的监督特征式文档修改法，第3节介绍并作为基线。近期有用LLM提示优化网页SEO的工作[3]，其提示为Google等商业搜索引擎设计，不太适合本文评估的一般排序函数；它们主要是零样本，不像本文包含历史排名例子。 另有针对BERT排序器的攻击[23]，以及针对LLM文档/商品排序器、对话代理和问答系统的攻击[9,14,17]，未必属于白帽。本文关注不绑定特定排序函数的白帽内容修改，评估同时涉及稠密与稀疏检索。 ### 2 文档修改方法 方法让LLM修改文档，使其在未知排序函数对某查询产生的下一轮排名中尽量靠前。假设可以观察该查询及其他查询的历史排序。另有两个目标：改稿有较高篇章质量，且内容尽可能忠于原文[6]。 提示由两部分组成：共用部分说明提升排名的改稿任务，并要求相似于原文；上下文专属部分提供历史排名信息。作者假设LLM在篇章表达上能产生高质量文本。 **共用提示全文：** ```text 编辑候选文档，改善它对候选查询的搜索排名，目标是最高名次（1为最高）。 利用用户提供的黑盒搜索引擎在多个查询上的历史排名作为上下文，指导编辑。 重点修改影响最大的句子，以增强排名潜力。 编辑后目标长度约为〈上下文文档语料的词数中位数〉，不超过150词。 确保改稿与候选原稿非常相似。 只生成编辑后的文档，不加额外评论或标题。 输入： - 候选查询： - 候选文档： ``` 词数中位数是后续上下文专属部分中所有文档词数的中位数。 **上下文专属部分。**为了给未知排序函数提供“线索”，引入四种历史信息，大多受到LLM排序提示研究[12,15,18]启发： - **Pointwise，逐点：**提供查询与此前排名第一文档的配对。它借鉴逐点评估中给予查询及相关/不相关文档示例的办法[11]。给出历史高排名文档，也类似竞争性搜索中常见的模仿高排名内容策略[7,19]。 - **Pairwise，成对：**提供查询与一对文档，并指出谁排名更高，受成对排序提示[18]启发。 - **Listwise，列表：**提供查询与整个有序文档列表，受列表式排序提示[12]启发。 - **Temporal，时序：**提供查询，以及同一文档不同历史版本和对应排名，帮助LLM理解修改怎样随时间影响排序。 **提示配置。**研究改变以下因素：查询数量；每查询示例数（逐点的历史第一文档数量、成对的文档对数、列表的列表数、时序的带变化历史文档数）；是否提供待改稿上轮名次；是否包括当前查询，还是只给其他查询；成对示例是随机两篇，还是第一名加随机另一篇；时序示例包含多少个历史名次。 ### 3 实验设置 #### 3.1 数据集与离线评估 数据来自排名竞赛[13,19]。学生被分配查询，撰写尽量排前的文档。第一轮前给查询相关的示例文档；之后每轮可观察自己的查询历史排名，再改稿争取下一轮改善。 **LambdaMARTComp。**由TREC9—TREC12 Web track的31个查询构成，每题5—6名学生竞争。隐藏排序函数是LambdaMART[4]，使用多种人工特征。依照Goren等[6]，取第7轮评估。其SentReplace作为基线：一种先进监督特征式改稿方法，用另一句替换原文一句，以同时提升排名、维持质量与忠实。 **脚注2：**原SentReplace使用SVMrank；作者发现换为LambdaMART效果更好，因此采用此版本。 **E5Comp。**竞赛隐藏函数是文档与查询E5向量[22]之间的余弦相似度。使用TREC9—TREC12中的15个查询，7轮，每查询4名玩家[21]。取第4轮评估，使改稿方法拥有足够历史。 **脚注3：**E5版本为 `intfloat/e5-large-unsupervised`，来源为Hugging Face。原文正文脚注排版中名称连字可能显示为“intﬂoat”，此处规范成可辨认标识。 两个数据集都将各改稿机器人用于指定轮的每篇非第一名文档。每次只改一篇：用该改稿，加上其他学生在下一轮真实提交的原文档版本，交给相同排序器重新排序。之后对所改文档及各查询求平均。不是一次把所有候选都交给机器人重写。 #### 3.2 评价指标 **归一化排名提升 Scaled Promotion。**遵照[6]，测下一轮相对当前轮名次的上升/下降，并分别除以最大可能上升/下降幅度。 **对原稿忠实。**比较改稿 (d_{mod}) 与原稿 (d_{curr})，使用Gekhman等[5]的自然语言推断 NLI 方法：判断作为假设的文档是否能被作为前提的另一文档蕴含，并保持事实一致。TrueTeacher 输出 (TT(premise,hypothesis)\in[0,1])，越高表示事实一致性越强。 先计算改稿句子中被原稿支持的平均比例，称原始忠实度 RF： \[ RF(d_{mod},d_{curr})=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^{n}\delta[TT(d_{curr},d_{mod}^{i})\ge0.5]. \] 其中 (d^i) 是第 (i) 句，\(\delta\) 为指示函数，满足条件取1，否则0。**脚注4：**依据[5]以0.5作为蕴含判定阈值。由于模型的 (RF(d_{curr},d_{curr})) 不一定为1，进一步归一化： \[ OrigFaith=\frac{RF(d_{mod},d_{curr})}{RF(d_{curr},d_{curr})}. \] **对语料忠实。**LLM改稿可能产生幻觉[20]，因此还衡量改稿与整个语料内容是否一致。把当前文档当查询，以余弦相似度检索语料中前 (k) 篇，检索集记 (T)；使用E5与TF.IDF两类表示。定义： \[ RCF(d_{mod})=\frac1{2k}\sum_{d\in T}\big[RF(d_{mod},d)+RF(d,d_{mod})\big], \qquad CF(d_{mod})=\frac{RCF(d_{mod})}{RCF(d_{curr})}. \] 分别得到CorpFaith(E5)与CorpFaith(TF.IDF)。**脚注5：**语料为评估轮之前所有轮的全部文档。**脚注6：**实验 (k=10)。 显著性使用双尾配对置换检验，100,000次随机置换，(p<0.05)。 #### 3.3 机器人实例化与筛选 改稿LLM为ChatGPT-4o[2]。查询数取{1,2}，每查询示例数{1,2,3}，时序历史轮数{2,3}，再结合前述二元配置，得到192种机器人提示。温度另取{0,0.5,1,1.5,2}[16]，用于控制潜在输出变化。 在两个数据集上，随机文档对的Pairwise和Listwise的Scaled Promotion最好；两者中各有一个相同配置始终进入两个数据集的前三名，说明跨LambdaMART与E5排序器有效。Temporal次之，但比Pointwise好。**脚注7：**作者因篇幅且认为不增加洞察，省略全部配置的实际数字；本稿不会补造排名。 后续展示两种配置：Pairwise只提供当前查询，每个最近三轮随机抽一对文档，不提供待改文档当前排名，温度0.5；Listwise只提供当前查询、前两轮列表，不提供待改稿当前排名，温度0。附录A给出提示。**脚注8：**这两个机器人在下面在线评估中也表现最好。 #### 3.4 在线评估 前述离线评估只有单轮，学生没有机会对机器人改稿后的排序作出反应。为此作者组织机器人与学生真正持续竞争的在线实验，类似Mordo等[13]，使用TREC9—TREC12的15个不同查询。 每局5名玩家：2—3名学生，一个Pairwise或Listwise机器人，以及1—2篇静态文档。静态内容的生成类似Raifer等[19]：在英文Wikipedia搜索查询，选高排名页，取不超过150词的段落，让3名标注者判相关性；不断重新提取，直到至少2名认为相关。选定段落随后作为该查询所有学生的静态文档。 学生不知道对手包含机器人。机器人在第5、6、7轮运行，报告三轮平均。**脚注9：**竞赛经机构与国际伦理委员会批准。**脚注10：**在线问题编号为21、55、61、64、74、75、83、96、124、144、161、164、166、170、194，与E5Comp不同。**脚注11：**技术问题导致不能像离线那样在第4轮运行。 相关性与质量由CloudResearch的Connect众包平台[1]评价。依先前工作[6,19]，5名英语标注者中至少3名认为文档有效、不是关键词堆砌或无用文本，质量记1，否则0。至少3名认为与问题相关，相关性记1，否则0。 ### 4 实验结果 **表1：LambdaMARTComp。**每次仅一篇由对应机器人改写，其余是学生下一轮文档。结果对所有非第一名目标与查询平均。学生的忠实指标跨实验块相同，因为使用同一批下一轮学生文档；学生的排名提升则受该块机器人改稿影响。原表r表示与SentReplace显著不同，s表示与学生显著不同；显著不同不等于更好，需结合数值。 |实验块|方法|Scaled Promotion|OrigFaith|CorpFaith(E5)|CorpFaith(TF.IDF)| |---|---|---|---|---|---| |SentReplace|SentReplace|0.309|0.786|0.468|0.381| |SentReplace|学生|0.313|0.727|0.544|0.504| |Pairwise|机器人|0.345（s）|0.57（s,r）|0.507|0.437| |Pairwise|学生|−0.095|0.727|0.544|0.504| |Listwise|机器人|0.315（s）|0.616（s,r）|0.497|0.427| |Listwise|学生|−0.09|0.727|0.544|0.504| Pairwise和Listwise排名提升超过SentReplace与同场学生。原稿忠实度低于学生及SentReplace，但作者认为仍较高。SentReplace只改一句，原文忠实度自然较高；两个LLM机器人的两类语料忠实度均高于SentReplace，因此即使使用LLM，其语料忠实度仍相对较高。 **表2：E5Comp。**s表示与学生显著不同。**脚注12：**从这里起不用SentReplace，因为该基线针对稀疏排序函数定义。 |实验块|方法|Scaled Promotion|OrigFaith|CorpFaith(E5)|CorpFaith(TF.IDF)| |---|---|---|---|---|---| |Pairwise|机器人|0.241（s）|0.623（s）|0.589|0.603| |Pairwise|学生|−0.107|0.788|0.531|0.542| |Listwise|机器人|0.341（s）|0.711|0.573|0.592| |Listwise|学生|−0.128|0.788|0.531|0.542| 在LambdaMARTComp上，机器人语料忠实度不超过学生；在E5Comp上，机器人排名提升和语料忠实度都超过学生，原稿忠实度则较低，作者仍称相对较高。两表共同显示对两种排序函数的有效性。 **表3：在线E5竞赛。**Q和R为跨文档、问题、第5—7轮平均质量/相关性。原图同时使用下标b和上标s，图注只解释s；以下保留b，不擅自认定其统计含义。 |竞赛机器人|方法|Scaled Promotion|OrigFaith|CorpFaith(E5)|CorpFaith(TF.IDF)|Q|R| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |Pairwise|机器人|0.098（b）|0.839（b）|0.663（b）|0.735（b）|0.822|0.8（b）| |Pairwise|学生|0.029|0.821|0.675|0.726|0.925|0.642| |Listwise|机器人|0.05|0.875（b）|0.717（b）|0.756（b）|0.911（s）|0.8（b）| |Listwise|学生|−0.013|0.865|0.685|0.754|0.732|0.66| 在线机器人排名提升、原稿忠实度及语料忠实度大多超过学生，语料指标有一个例外。Listwise生成文档平均质量比同场学生高；Pairwise场次中学生质量更高，但机器人82.2%的文档仍被判高质量。两个机器人相关性合格的比例都高于学生。 作者总体认为，机器人在排名提升、内容质量和相关性、语料忠实度等多个维度相对学生与SentReplace具有明确价值。 ![[附件_11/原文第4页.png]] ### 5 结论 本文提出用LLM提示修改文档，使其在未知排序函数对查询的排序中提高名次。部分方法受到LLM排序提示启发。通过两个排序器的历史竞赛数据，以及机器人和学生的在线竞赛广泛评估，表现最好的改稿方法相对学生和先前高效特征式方法展现优势。 ### 附录 A 提示词 下列为共用提示之后的上下文部分。将原图字符串中的 `\n` 展开为实际换行，所有占位文档与名次保留。 **图1：Pairwise完整上下文。**分别从最近三次排序随机抽(a,b)、(c,d)、(e,f)两篇，并注明各自名次。 ```text 查询： * 文档： 最近一次排名： * 文档： 最近一次排名： 查询： * 文档： 倒数第二次排名： * 文档： 倒数第二次排名： 查询： * 文档： 倒数第三次排名： * 文档： 倒数第三次排名： ``` **图2：Listwise完整上下文。**最近一轮列表a—d排除当前待改稿，前一轮e—i包含全列表。原图 `DOCUMNET b` 是占位符拼写错误，本译文规范为文档b，不改变内容。 ```text 查询： * 以下文档按最近一轮针对该查询的名次，从高到低排列： * * * * * 以下文档按倒数第二轮针对该查询的名次，从高到低排列： 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. ``` Wu等，2023：PRADA：针对神经排序模型的实用黑盒对抗攻击。 ## 第二部分：详细解释与小白实操教学 ### 1. 先分清它解决的是哪一关 这篇不是“让AI在回答里引用我”的直接实验，而是“给定几篇候选，改稿后能否排得更高”。排序器是LambdaMART或E5，不是公开ChatGPT、Google整个产品。虽然改稿LLM为4o，最终排名也不是由4o生成。把“用LLM改稿”误写成“LLM搜索推荐实测”，会改变论文研究对象。 它能给GEO学习者的启发是：只给模型一句“帮我优化”信息很少；加入与你实际目标相同的历史比较样本，可能让改稿更有方向。但这份证据仍限于文中的短文竞赛与排序器。 ### 2. 四种上下文用一个例子讲清 假设查询“怎么清洁不锈钢保温杯”。A文讲清洗顺序与不适用情况，B文主要宣传产品，C文有完整步骤却夹很多无关内容。 |方法|你给改稿工具看什么|它可能学到什么|风险| |---|---|---|---| |Pointwise|“A上轮第一”|第一名长什么样|不知道A因何胜出，容易盲目模仿| |Pairwise|“A第1、B第4”|相关两篇差异|差异可能来自别的变量，不能当因果证明| |Listwise|“A、C、B完整排序”|不同层次的相对特征|输入长，混杂因素更多| |Temporal|“B改前第4、改后第2”|某次修改与名次变化|对手也在改，变动不能都归因于B| 以上只是自拟示意，不是论文样本。论文发现Pairwise/Listwise较好，不意味着你的行业永远同样，更不意味着复制第一名内容。学习结构与信息覆盖，与复制别人原句不是同一操作。 ### 3. 第2节的150词是不是通用SEO要求 不是。竞赛文档很短，静态段落也限制150词，提示才如此设计。不能据此把一篇需要解释机制的3,000字教程硬压成150词，也不能把英语词数直接等同中文字符数。迁移时应保留真实任务所需信息，用合理的同类篇幅作约束，并报告这是教学改编、不是原设置复现。 “非常相似于原文”也只是提示要求，不能自动保证忠实。表1的机器人OrigFaith反而低于学生和单句替换基线，说明需要独立检查。 ### 4. 第3节怎么评估排名提升 为便于理解，若5篇候选中原第4、新第2，上升2名，最多能升3名，Scaled Promotion为2/3≈0.667。若原第2、新第4，下降2名，最多可降3名，得−2/3。实际计算应处理边界位置，并以原评估实现为准。 因此0.345不是“平均名次上升0.345名”，也不是“流量增长34.5%”。它是标准化排名变化的平均。表1不同块学生排名不同，是因为机器人改稿改变了竞争，而学生忠实度相同是因为拿的是同一组学生文档。 **练习。**原第5、新第3、候选共6篇，上升2/4=0.5。原第3、新第5，下降−2/3≈−0.667。这说明同样两名的升降，归一化值可能不同。 ### 5. RF、OrigFaith与CorpFaith有什么区别 RF问：“改稿每个句子，原稿支持吗？”假设改稿4句，3句被TrueTeacher判原稿支持，RF=0.75。原稿自检RF=0.8，则OrigFaith=0.75/0.8=0.9375。它是相对于模型自检基准的比值，不是人类认证“93.75%的内容一定正确”。因分母可小于1，理论上可能超过1，不能直接解释成概率。 CorpFaith问：“改稿与历史语料彼此支持吗？”先取10篇接近的历史文档，再做双向RF并平均，最后除以原稿的同类值。E5和TF.IDF是两种选择邻近文档的方法，不是两个独立人工事实核查团队。 **关键区别。**原稿漏了一个事实，改稿从其他历史材料补上，可能对语料更忠实、对原稿更不忠实；但如果历史语料本身错，彼此一致不代表现实正确。对外发布前仍需核验具体证据。 **小练习：**原稿“这个方法适用于无涂层杯体，先阅读说明书”；改稿删去“无涂层”并补“适用于所有杯子”。即便更像高排名文档，也发生了范围扩大。要在新增/删除清单里标出，不能只看词面相似。 ### 6. 第4节的结果怎么避免误读 离线LambdaMART中Pairwise排名提升0.345对SentReplace0.309，但OrigFaith0.57对0.786。这是收益与忠实度代价并存。s/r标记仅说明差异达到设定统计标准，低值也会显著。 在线Pairwise的质量0.822低于学生0.925；Listwise的质量0.911高于同场学生0.732。不能一句“机器人质量全面胜过人类”概括。两个实验块的学生与比赛条件不完全相同，也不宜直接用两个机器人Q值相减来证明Listwise普遍更好。 “在线”在这里是作者组织的动态竞赛，不是把网页发布到真实Google后观察SEO。学生可以回应对手，确实比离线多一层互动，但仍是小规模、有限查询、特定排序器。 ### 7. 不写代码也能学的改稿流程 以下为教学应用，未替你实际跑排名实验： 1. 选你拥有且有明确目标的一段内容，固定真实问题，例如“如何整理Obsidian论文笔记”。保留原稿A。 2. 收集同一目标、同一排序环境、同一时期可观察的历史案例。不能把不同产品的排名混在一起却不标来源。 3. 先用Pairwise方式写出两个例子及实际顺序；不知道真实排名就标“人工偏好示例”，不要编成搜索证据。 4. 要求改稿工具只改变表达与结构，并列出所有新增事实、删除限制。原论文只输出改稿；这份差异清单是教学增加的审核层。 5. 人工检查原稿关键点、条件、例外是否保留。无来源内容退回，不因行文流畅就接受。 6. 在固定候选、同一评价方法下比较A/B，另看质量与相关性。如果是观察公开搜索，要记录时间、地区、候选变化；不能把一次名次波动认定为改稿效果。 **示范指令（教学版）：** ```text 目标问题：如何整理Obsidian论文笔记？ 原稿：<粘贴本人原稿> 历史比较样本：<真实文档摘要、顺序、观察日期与环境> 请参考样本的信息组织改写，但不得复制样本文句、编造排名、添加原稿没有依据的事实。 保留操作前提、限制与来源。输出改稿和逐项修改理由，并单列需要我核验的内容。 ``` 假如原稿有“只在同一个库里测试过链接”，改稿必须保留这个边界，不能升级成“所有平台自动同步”。这比单纯要求“写得权威”更能避免失真。 ### 8. 小白验收表与边界 |验收项|具体检查| |---|---| |证据真实|历史名次、查询、日期有记录，不伪造| |内容忠实|关键点与限制逐项比对，新增知识有出处| |质量|步骤能看懂，非关键词堆砌，无意义句子删除| |相关性|直接解决目标问题，非为了排名改成别的话题| |效果|同一设置比较，报告前后值及失败例子| |适用范围|短文排序结果不扩张为整站流量或AI引用承诺| 论文没有给出全部192种配置的具体成绩，没有展示长期商业站点流量，也没有给公开生成式回答的引用测试。表3的b标记含义未解释；年份页眉与arXiv信息冲突。这些都在本稿保留为证据边界，不能靠“白帽”标题推断每份输出都已核验。 ### 自测 **为什么只给第一名不一定最好？**没有相对失败例子，难判断哪些差异重要；论文在该设置发现Pairwise/Listwise表现更好。 **OrigFaith高是不是事实绝对正确？**不是，只是相对原稿的模型判定；原稿可能有错。 **机器人比学生升得多，能不能直接替代审核？**不能，部分忠实度和质量指标更低，需同时检查。 **这篇能不能直接证明我会被ChatGPT引用？**不能，它测的是LambdaMART/E5候选排序。学到的是有上下文、保留语义、独立评价的改稿方法。 ## ABSTRACT
We present novel white-hat search engine optimization techniques
based on genAI and demonstrate their empirical merits.
1
INTRODUCTION
In competitive search settings [10], document authors might re-
spond to rankings induced for queries of interest by modifying
their documents. The goal is to improve future ranking. These
modiﬁcations are often referred to as search engine optimization
(SEO) [8]. Our focus, as that of prior work on competitive search
[6, 10, 19], is on white hat SEO [8]: legitimate document modiﬁca-
tions which do not hurt document quality nor the search ecosys-
tem.
We present novel document modiﬁcation methods for ad hoc re-
trieval that are based on prompting large language models (LLMs).
The desiderata of the modiﬁcations are (cf., [6]): (i) potentially im-
proving future ranking for a query at hand, (ii) maintaining “faith-
fulness” to the original document, and (iii) producing a document
of high (content) quality. Some of our methods are inspired by re-
cent work on using prompting techniques to have LLMs induce
rankings in response to queries [11, 12, 18]. For example, some of
the prompts include information induced from past rankings to
provide the LLM with implicit information about the undisclosed
ranking function.
We evaluate the document modiﬁcation methods using datasets
that resulted from past ranking competitions [13, 19]. In addition,
we organized ranking competitions and used our modiﬁcation meth-
ods as bots competing against humans1. The empirical evaluation
demonstrates the merits of the most eﬀective methods we studied
with respect to humans and to a highly eﬀective feature-based ap-
proach for document modiﬁcation [6].
Related work. We refer the reader to [10] for a survey on com-
petitive search. The work most related to ours is that of Goren et
al. [6] who devised a supervised feature-based document modiﬁ-
cation method. We discuss the method in Section 3 and use it as a
baseline.
1The dataset of the competition we organized, and the accompanying code, will be
made public upon publication of this paper. They are available for reviewing purposes
at https://github.com/promptdriven2025.
There is recent work on performing SEO for Web pages by prompt-
ing LLMs [3]. The prompts are designed for commercial search en-
gines such as Google and are not well suited to the general rank-
ing functions we use for evaluation. In addition, the prompts, in
contrast to ours, do not include examples of past rankings and are
mainly zero shot.
There is work on attacks (not necessarily white hat) on BERT-
based document rankers (e.g., [23]) and on LLM-based document
and product rankers, conversational agents and question answer-
ing systems (e.g., [9, 14, 17]). Our focus, in contrast, is on white hat
content modiﬁcation for document ranking which is not commit-
ted to a speciﬁc ranking function. We focus on dense and sparse
retrieval in our evaluation.
2
DOCUMENT MODIFICATION METHODS
We present methods utilizing a large language model (LLM) that
modify a document so as to have it highly ranked in the next rank-
ing induced for a query by an undisclosed ranking function. We
assume that past rankings for the query and other queries can be
observed. We post two additional goals for the modiﬁcation: hav-
ing the resultant document of high quality (in terms of discourse)
and as “faithful” as possible to the original document in terms of
the content it contains [6].
The modiﬁcation methods are based on prompting an LLM. The
prompts have two parts: (i) a general shared part which describes
the task (document modiﬁcation for improved ranking) with a di-
rective to maintain similarity to the original document (i.e., faith-
fulness); and, (ii) context-speciﬁc part, speciﬁc to a prompt, which
provides information about past rankings. We assume that the LLM
produces high quality content in terms of discourse. The general
shared part is:
Edit the candidate document to improve its search engine rank-
ing for the candidate query, aiming for the highest rank (1 being the
highest). Use the black box search engine’s past rankings over various
queries, provided as context by the user, to guide your edits. Focus on
editing the most impactful sentences to enhance ranking potential.
Target an edited document length of around «median length of con-
text document corpus» words, not exceeding 150 words. Ensure the
edited document is very similar to the candidate document. Generate
only the edited document, without additional comments or titles.
Input:
- Candidate Query: <query>

Bardas et al/.
- Candidate Document: <current document>
The placeholder: «median length of context document» is the
median number of words in documents provided in the context-
speciﬁc part of the prompt that follows the general part.
Context-speciﬁc part. The goal of this part of the prompt is to
provide the LLM with “hints” about the undisclosed ranking func-
tion; speciﬁcally, past rankings. We present four types of context,
most of which are inspired by work on using LLMs to induce rank-
ing [12, 15, 18].
• Pointwise: The context includes pairs of a query and a doc-
ument which was the highest ranked in the past for the
query. This context is inspired by pointwise approaches to
LLM ranking which provide the LLM with a query and ex-
amples of relevant and non-relevant documents (e.g., [11]).
Including the documents most highly ranked in the past for
the query at hand is conceptually reminiscent of a preva-
lent document modiﬁcation strategy in competitive search
[7, 19]: mimicking content in the most highly ranked docu-
ments in the past.
• Pairwise: Inspired by work on using pairwise approaches
to prompt an LLM to induce ranking [18], the context in-
cludes queries accompanied with pairs of documents and
an indication about which was ranked higher.
• Listwise: Inspired by listwise prompting approaches for LLM
ranking [12], the context includes queries and ranked docu-
ment lists.
• Temporal: The context includes a query and versions of the
same document and their ranks in past rankings induced for
the query. The goal is to provide the LLM with information
about how modiﬁcations of a document aﬀected its ranking
along time.
Prompt conﬁgurations. There are numerous conﬁgurations of
the context-speciﬁc part that we study. These are determined by
the following factors and parameters: (i) the number of queries
used; (ii) the number of examples used per query: number of the
most highest ranked documents in the past (Pointwise), number
of pairs (Pairwise), number of ranked lists (Listwise) and number
of documents with their temporal changes and ranks (Temporal);
(iii) whether the rank of the document to be modiﬁed in the last
ranking induced for the query is included; (iv) whether the query at
hand is included in the prompt, or alternatively only other queries;
(v) for the pairwise approach (Pairwise) we consider a random se-
lection of the pair of documents or the highest ranked document
and an additional randomly selected document; and, (vi) for the
Temporal approach (Temporal), we vary the number of past ranks
of the example document.
3
EXPERIMENTAL SETTINGS
Datasets. We use datasets which are reports of ranking compe-
titions [13, 19]. In these competitions, students were assigned to
queries and had to produce documents that wouldbe highly ranked.
Before the ﬁrst round the students were provided with an exam-
ple of a document relevant to the query. In each of the following
rounds, the students observed past rankings for their queries and
could modify their documents to potentially improve their next
round ranking.
The ﬁrst dataset, LambdaMARTComp, is the result of rank-
ing competitions held for 31 queries from the TREC9-TREC12 Web
tracks [19]. Five to six students competedfor each query. The undis-
closed ranking function was LambdaMART [4] applied with vari-
ous hand-crafted features. Following Goren et al. [6], whose docu-
ment modiﬁcation approach, SentReplace, serves as a baseline2,
we use round 7 for evaluation [19]. SentReplace is a state-of-the-
art feature-based supervised method for ranking-incentivized doc-
ument modiﬁcation. It replaces a sentence in the document with
another sentence to improve ranking and to maintain content qual-
ity and faithfulness to the original document.
The second dataset, E5Comp, is a report of ranking compe-
titions [13] where the undisclosed ranking function was the co-
sine between the E5 embedding vectors [22] of a document and a
query3. The competitions were run for 7 rounds with 15 queries
from the Web tracks of TREC9-TREC12; 4 players were competing
for each query [21]. We used round 4 for evaluation to allow the
document modiﬁcation methods to have enough history of past
rankings.
For both datasets just described, we apply the diﬀerent docu-
ment modiﬁcation methods, henceforth referred to as bots, upon
each of the documents in the ranked list for a query in the speciﬁed
round (except for the highest ranked document). For each selected
document, we induce a ranking using the same ranker used in the
competitions over its modiﬁed version and the original next-round
versions of the other documents (of students) from the round. We
use the evaluation measures described below upon the resultant
ranking. We average the evaluation results across all documents
we modiﬁed per round and over queries.
Evaluation measures. To evaluate rank promotion (demotion) of
documents as a result of modiﬁcation, we follow Goren et al. [6]
and report Scaled Promotion: the increase (decrease) of rank in
the next round with respect to the current round normalized by
the maximum possible rank promotion (demotion).
To evaluate the faithfulness of a modiﬁed document (푑푚표푑) to its
original (current) version (푑푐푢푟푟), we compare the two documents
using Gekhman’s et al. [5] natural language inference (NLI) ap-
proach. Speciﬁcally, we estimate whether one document (denoted
hypothesis) is entailed from the other document (denoted premise)
while preserving factual consistency. The estimate is the TT (TrueTeacher)
measure: TT(푝푟푒푚푖푠푒,ℎ푦푝표푡ℎ푒푠푖푠) is the output of the model in the
range [0,1]; higher scores indicate stronger factual alignment.
To apply the TrueTeacher model, we ﬁrst compute the average
number of sentences in the modiﬁed document that are entailed4
by the current document, which we refer to as raw faithfulness

Instantiating bots. For LLM we use Chat-GPT 4o [2]. As described

Rank promotion performance of bots. In terms of Scaled Pro-
motion, we found7 that the Pairwise bots (with random selection
of document pairs) and the Listwise bots were the best performing
for both the LambdaMARTComp and E5Comp datasets; the same
speciﬁc instantiation of each of these two bots was always among
the top-3 performing bots for both datasets. This ﬁnding attests to
the rank-promotion eﬀectiveness of these types of bots (prompts)
for diﬀerent rankers (LambdaMART and E5). The Temporal bots
(prompts), which provide rank-changes information along rounds,
were less eﬀective (in terms of Scaled Promotion) than the Pair-
wise and Listwise bots, but were more eﬀective than the Pointwise
bots.
In what follows, we present the evaluation of the two bots which
posted for both datasets Scaled Promotion among the best three:8
• Pairwise, where only the given query is included, one ran-
dom pair of documents for each of the three last rounds is
provided as examples, the current rank of the document is
not used, and the temperature is set to 0.5.
• Listwise, where only the given query is included, two pre-
vious rounds are used, the current rank is not used, and the
temperature is set to 0.
Appendix A provides the prompts for these bots.

Online evaluation. The evaluation performed over the LambdaMART-
Comp and E5Comp datasets is oﬄine and therefore spans a single
round: the students who competed in the competition did not re-
spond to rankings induced over the documents we modify here.
We therefore also performed online evaluation where our instan-
tiated prompts competed as bots against students. We organized a
ranking competition9 similar to that of Mordo et al. [13] using 15
queries from TREC9-TREC1210. In contrast to Mordo et al.’s compe-
titions [13], each game included 5 players: two-three students, one
of the two bots discussed above (Pairwise or Listwise), and one or
two static documents were created using a procedure similar to
the one in Raifer et al. [19]: ﬁrst, we used the query in the Eng-
lish Wikipedia search engine and selected a highly ranked page.
We then extracted a candidate paragraph from this page, with a
length of up to 150 words. Three annotators assessed the relevance
of the passages, and we repeated the extraction process for each
query until at least two annotators judged a paragraph as relevant.
The selected paragraph was then used as a static document for the
query for all students.
The students were not aware that they were competing against
bots. We applied our bots in rounds 511, 6 and 7 and report the
average performance over these three rounds.
We had documents in the online evaluation judged for relevance
and quality using crowdsourcing annotators on the Connect plat-
form of CloudResearch [1]. Following past work on ranking com-
petitions [6, 19], a document’s quality grade is set to 1 if at least
three out of ﬁve English-speaking annotators marked it as valid
(as opposed to keyword stuﬀed or useless) and to 0 otherwise. The
relevance grade was 1 if the document was marked relevant by at
least three annotators and 0 otherwise.
4
EXPERIMENTAL RESULTS
Table 1 presents the evaluation over the LambdaMARTComp. We
let one of our bots, or the baseline bot, SentReplace [6], modify a
single document at a time. We then analyze the resultant ranking
over the single modiﬁed document and the next-round students’
documents from the dataset. The performance numbers are aver-
ages over the diﬀerent selected documents to be modiﬁed (all but
the highest ranked one) and over queries. Note that the Students’
faithfulness values are not block dependent as they are the same in
all three cases in the next round. Their Scaled Promotion is aﬀected
by the bot used to modify the selected document.
Table 1 shows that our Pairwise and Listwise bots outperform
SentReplace and the students in terms of Scaled Promotion. The
faithfulness of both of our bots is lower than that of the students
and SentReplace but is still quite high. Note that SentReplace mod-
iﬁes a single sentence in a document and, hence, the modiﬁed doc-
ument is quite faithful to the original document. The corpus faith-
fulness of both our bots (for both TF.IDF and E5) is higher than
that of SentReplace. Thus, although our bots use an LLM (as op-
posed to SentReplace and the students), their corpus faithfulness
is relatively high.

of our bots with respect to students and the SentReplace baseline
along various dimensions; speciﬁcally, rank promotion, document
quality and relevance, and faithfulness to the corpus.

ranking function for a query. Our methods are based on prompting
large language models (LLMs). Some of our methods are inspired
